name: Kerberoasting - Service Ticket Requested for User SPN
description: Kerberoasting is a Credential Access technique that hands the attacker an offline-crackable password hash for a service account.
note:
## Triage

1. Expand the alert. Read `winlog.event_data.ServiceName` — this is the account whose password hash the attacker now has offline. In this lab that's `svc_sql` (SPN `MSSQLSvc/sql.lab.local:1433`).
2. Check `winlog.event_data.TargetUserName` (who requested the ticket) and `winlog.event_data.IpAddress` (from which host). A workstation requesting a service account's ticket is suspicious; that account's own app server is not.
3. Check `winlog.event_data.TicketEncryptionType`. `0x17` (RC4) is a strong attack signal — tools force RC4 to crack faster. `0x12` (AES256) does NOT clear the alert: this lab's DC issues AES, so the attack looks "normal" on encryption alone.
4. Look for a burst: many 4769 for different SPNs from one account in seconds means SPN enumeration (Atomic test 5 requests every SPN at once).
5. Confirm whether the requestor normally talks to this service. If not, treat as credential theft in progress and rotate the service account's password.

## Notes

- Fires on any service ticket (4769) for an SPN owned by a user account, excluding computer accounts (`*$`) and `krbtgt` — the accounts that make up all normal 4769 traffic.
- Does not rely on encryption type, on purpose (see triage step 3).
- Detection lands on DC01 (the KDC), not on the host the attack ran from.

## Known false positives

- A legitimate application or admin requesting a real service account's ticket. Validate the requestor and source host before closing.

## Validation

Atomic Red Team T1558.003 test 5 (Request All Tickets via PowerShell), run as a domain principal. Verified 2026-10-10: `svc_sql` 4769 observed on DC01.
query: host.name : "dc01" and event.code : "4769" and not winlog.event_data.ServiceName : *$ and not winlog.event_data.ServiceName : "krbtgt"
